messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after flipping default kernel to flashv3 on apac-h100 for redwood-13b-q8 we saw an unexpected p95 regression (~+18%) vs triton. logged it in the test run below, not huge but consistent across 4 runs :thinking_face:

sam: ugh. are we talking long-sequence or small payloads?

maria: small payloads primarily. seq=64 median payloads, bursty single-request traffic. config used:
```bash
run_bench --model redwood-13b --kernel flashv3 --quant q8 --batch 1 --seq 64 --warmup 100 --measure p95,p50 --region apac
```

maria: sample summary (apac/h100/flashv3):
```
p50  28ms
p95  142ms
throughput ~350rps
```

maria: same run with triton-vendor-kernels on the same machines:
```
p50  30ms
p95  120ms
throughput ~330rps
```

yuki: interesting — flashv3 giving better p50 but worse tail. could be packing/warmup or kernel path for tiny batches. did you check kernel selection logs?

maria: yes, runtime picked flashv3 fastpath for small batch, but I see more context-switching and NVTX traces show repeated kernel launches for attention fragments. suspect memory fragmentation + driver differences in APAC images.

dana: note: APAC cluster recently updated to driver 535.54 while US/EU are on 535.45. there was a cuBLASLt patch in 535.5x that changed small-matrix scheduling. could be the culprit.

liam: oh right — vendor kernel fallback path uses a different GEMM tiling when cuBLASLt reports workspace limits. flashv3 tries to allocate larger temp buffers and falls back to smaller kernels that increase launch count.

sam: can we reproduce by forcing different driver on a single box or by toggling flashv3 fastpath?

maria: repro plan I ran locally: swap driver to 535.54 in eu sandbox (same HW) and re-run. also tried toggling flashv3 microbatching off with env var:
```bash
export FLASHV3_MICROBATCH=0
run_bench ...
```
result: p95 improved ~10ms but still worse than triton.

yuki: please also collect nvprof traces and kernel names. if we see lots of small GEMMs instead of one big GEMM that points at tiling mismatch.

infra-bot: scheduled job #bench-2781234567-nvprof on apac-h100 (ETA 12m). logs link: https://ci.redwood/bench/2781234567

dana: action items from infra: pin APAC driver to 535.45 on a canary pool, run 24h smoke to ensure no other regressions.

maria: ML action items: 1) run nvprof & nvtx traces, 2) collect opt-level kernel selection logs, 3) try flashv3 with reduced workspace and microbatch off, 4) quick triton-vs-flash A/B in apac canary pool.

liam: heuristic idea: for small-payload low-latency SLOs, prefer kernel path that minimizes kernel-launch-count even if single-GEMM latency is marginally higher. that means our switcher should consider p95 penalty under live qshape distribution, not just p50.

sam: agree. we should add a new metric to kernel-decision: p95_delta_when_traffic=small_payload_ratio>0.5. guardrail before global switchover.

maria: will add a quick eval harness that runs 1000 single-request synthetic samples (seq 8..128) and computes p50/p95 delta per kernel+driver. I can land a PR to runtime switcher rules after results.

yuki: if you need help writing the nvprof parser ping me. I'll also check if quantized GEMM codepath differs by driver.

maria: thanks all. leaving infra-bot job to finish; will post results in this thread when nvprof is ready. :thumbsup:
